sites.name: Skull Creek dunes, Catlow Valley
sites.inspection: Author original-fall estimate distinguished from mapped reworked accumulation
sites.preservation: Published1986, not1996 as some repository metadata states. Most mapped ash-rich sediments contain less than10% unmixed primary ash; 25 cm mixed deposit is excluded. Do not multiply this percentage into a thickness. Quantitative basis of original estimate is not fully documented; test isolated omission and a weaker10 cm upper ceiling. If two falls include a precursor, an upper bound on their nonnegative sum also bounds the climactic share. Exact decimal typography pending.
sites.control: Principal CSV contains this upper estimate once; no visibility sensitivity calibration inferred
sites.reference: Mehringer and Wigand1986, Journal of Arid Environments11:117–138, doi:10.1016/S0140-1963(18)31224-2

sites.name: Deep Creek peat pit, North Okanagan
sites.horizon: 70 cm ash between two original radiocarbon samples
sites.inspection: 70 cm ash between 65–70 cm and 75–80 cm organic muck; separate ash at 40 cm and marl at 50 cm.
sites.preservation: A bed lying wholly between those samples can occupy at most 75 minus 70 cm. Undetected dispersed ash, substantial loss, compaction or a different ash identity could invalidate transfer to primary bulk fallout. Older drainage-channel setting; do not use the 40 or 70 cm depths as thickness.
sites.control: The bracketing non-target horizons are in the same vertical section. A weaker response and omission are tested.
sites.reference: Dyck, Fyles and Blake 1965, Geological Survey of Canada Radiocarbon Dates IV, doi:10.1017/S0033822200037061

sites.name: Medicine Lake, B100NC-1
sites.inspection: Ash 147.5 cm. Non-target levels 137.5 and 151.25 cm bracket it.
sites.preservation: Requires correct stratigraphy, capture of primary fallout within the bracket and negligible loss/compaction for transfer to original thickness. Use a lake station as location proxy, not the volcano summit; double bound and omit in sensitivities.
sites.control: The bracketing non-target horizons are in the same vertical section. A weaker response and omission are tested.
sites.reference: Nathenson, Donnelly-Nolan, Champion and Lowenstern 2007, USGS SIR 2007-5174-B, Table 2, drawing on Starratt et al. 2003 and Lowenstern microprobe data

sites.name: Mahoney Lake, deep basin
sites.inspection: Heinrichs et al. Methods, Dating, Table 1; Overmann et al. Fig.3 and pp.36–37; BC Geographic Names 3956
sites.preservation: Assumes primary fallout was sufficiently retained in this interval at the deep meromictic basin and bulk compaction/loss is negligible. Prolonged enrichment and other descriptions of 70–80 cm make the conversion conditional. Compare weaker upper and omission.
sites.control: Original source delineates the preserved ash package; retain a weaker upper and omit in independent refits.
sites.reference: Heinrichs et al. 1997, Midge- and diatom-based palaeosalinity reconstructions for Mahoney Lake; Lowe et al. 1997, Holocene fluctuations of a meromictic lake in southern British Columbia; Overmann et al. 1993, Fossil carotenoids and paleolimnology of meromictic Mahoney Lake

sites.name: Lodgepole Quarry
sites.horizon: ash deposit on Suttle Lake outwash soil
sites.inspection: Day 3 Stop 2, Suttle Lake outwash, p.51; 9.9 mi road-log turn
sites.preservation: An approximate field ceiling. Requires retention of the climactic deposit and negligible net thinning/compaction; earlier or imported material could inflate the total. Double the ceiling and omit in sensitivities; exact face offset from the turnoff unreported.
sites.control: Original source delineates the preserved ash package; retain a weaker upper and omit in independent refits.
sites.reference: Scott, Gardner and Sarna-Wojcicki (eds.) 1989, Guidebook for Field Trip to the Mount Bachelor–South Sister–Bend Area, USGS OFR 89-645

sites.name: Simon Young Site 24
sites.horizon: Mazama correlation of the cited investigators.
sites.inspection: Sheet1 row 16; Young Table 1.1 row 24 and Fig. 1.14
sites.preservation: Use Young’s published upper equivalent if the original target mass is represented by the site estimate and original bulk density is at least 700 kg/m³. Lower density or net export can violate this ceiling. Other additive phases or imported material can inflate the ceiling.
sites.control: Source estimate and original-to-preserved transfer. No separate scenario likelihood at this site.

sites.name: Jesmond Bog
sites.horizon: Mathews reports Mazama glass in the peat section. Lowdon and Blake give a tentative Mazama identification for this same depth.
sites.inspection: Jesmond Borehole #2, 500 ft from north edge, 433 cm. GSC-511 and GSC-529 p. 227. Williams and Goles pp. 37–38. Young p. 29.
sites.preservation: Use Young’s published upper equivalent if the original target mass is represented by the site estimate and original bulk density is at least 700 kg/m³. Lower density or net export can violate this ceiling. Other additive phases or imported material can inflate the ceiling. The upper endpoint additionally assumes no material lost by coring. Try the author’s original 0.5 cm estimate separately.
sites.control: Source estimate and original-to-preserved transfer. No separate scenario likelihood at this site.
sites.reference: Mathews in Williams and Goles 1968 pp. 37–38, Lowdon and Blake 1968 p. 227, Young 1990 Table 1.1 site 12

sites.name: Willapa Canyon terrace, Brown Bear BB326-36-PC
sites.archive: Marine sediment on a canyon-head terrace, offshore Washington.
sites.horizon: Mostly glass layer historically correlated to Mazama. A primary fall origin remains possible. The terrain and overlying section differ from nearby ash-bearing turbidites.
sites.inspection: Williams and Goles p. 37 give the 4 cm bed. Goldfinger et al. section on storm triggering identifies core and 240 cm depth. USGS usSEABED Pacific extracted table station BB326-36-PC.
sites.preservation: Possible canyon transport, compaction, winnowing or incomplete retention could invalidate transfer to original airborne bulk. Compare omission. The mixed marine blanket has no positive numerical primary minimum.
sites.control: Source estimate and original-to-preserved transfer. No separate scenario likelihood at this site.
sites.reference: Royse 1967, Northwest Science 41, 103–109. Williams and Goles 1968 pp. 37–38 and map. Goldfinger et al. 2012, USGS PP 1661-F.
